# Policy-KB bijection audit — host_payout_desk / task 0

(corpus sha256 `7da246892cebe4ab93b6ac459233c4454f351cd6b2e7d878c86f5214a4940f6b`).
Blind answer frozen at `audits/runtime_context/host_payout_desk/0.md` **before** any source-layer
artefact was opened; this file is written after the reveal.

**Entry conditions (checked, not re-run).** The brief supplies: the policy-side verdict for this
difficulty is PASS on both tasks and all four relationships at round 3; `check_docs.py … payouts`
is green (`docs=54 roles={'hub':5,'factor':23,'facet':10,'policy':11,'baseline':5}`,
`required quantitative keys=134  task_tools=5  prerequisite edges=3`, all mechanical gates PASS,
semantic bijection flagged `[MANUAL REQUIRED]`); `check_traceability.py … host_payout_desk` is green
(`0.json 17 copied / 0 missing`). The runtime-visible view and a tool-shaped DB access path were both
supplied and used. No input was missing.

Task 0's domain is the three extended policies of its tree — `payouts_ext_requested_draw`,
`payouts_ext_claim_reserve_release`, `payouts_ext_recovery_correction` — every base policy governing
their subjects, the `Keyturn Instant Payout Schedule` variant parameters they read, and their three
task-tool contracts. The scan below nevertheless sweeps the product's whole normative domain, because
untriggered branches count.

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the 54 documents was traced to a structured source. Obligations, eligibility
tests, prohibitions, calculations, waits, orderings, owner statements and terminal states all resolve to a
base policy clause, an extended policy rule, a `baseline.rule`, a factor ladder, a variant parameter, an
eligibility evidence contract, a `state_contract`, or a task-tool contract in `task_tools.py`.

**Additions found: none of substance.** In particular, the corpus contains no "please confirm the amount
with the customer", no "review again before handling", no "notify the host after completion", no "if it
fails, follow some procedure". The hubs' *Points of judgement* sections restate their own rule's clauses
(e.g. "Is the earlier entry changed? No. It is left exactly as it stands" ← "the original entry is never
edited"); the facet documents' *Points of judgement* restate their own tables.

**Rewrites found: one**, recorded in `bijection_verdict`.

**Omissions found: none.** Every clause of every base policy in the domain, every sentence of the three
baseline rules, every tier of all 23 ladders except the one noted, every variant parameter and every
eligibility evidence contract has a prose home.

**Tool fidelity.** The three hub documents' parameter tables and Return sections match `task_tools.py`
exactly in name, type, format ("a positive number rounded half to even to 2 decimal places; there is no
empty value and no currency conversion"), owner and effect. The written effects are the tools' real
effects: `release_claim_reserve_fb50cb2e` updates `reserve_balance` only, matching "the balance held in
reserve falls by that sum while the total credited stays as it was"; `post_recovery_correction_f20745c1`
raises `available_balance`, matching "the account's balance rises by the sum put back";
`release_host_payout_draw_8e4fb8ab` lowers it and books `payout_method="ach_standard"`, matching "as a
standard bank transfer". The `"pyt_"/"pyc_"/"pyl_"` id prefixes are correctly left out.

**Prerequisite-side check 1 — cross-problem operational guidance: none found.** No document contains
"first call …", "see also", "set out elsewhere", "resolved before", "must be resolved" or any equivalent;
a targeted scan of twenty routing phrasings returned nothing. Each of the five task tool names appears in

## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION RED — one defect, in a policy of this task's tree.**

### R1. A tier condition's window changed from three months to one month

- **Symptom.** *Measuring the Routine Reserve Standing on a Keyturn Host Payout Account*
  (`which_routine_reserves_count_as_standing_b4e2adac.json`) decides which of its three tiers governs by
  asking whether a reserve has been freed **in the month up to that day**. The source asks whether one has
  been freed **in the last three months**.
- **Root cause.** The factor `routine_reserve_measure` of `payouts_ext_claim_reserve_release` binds
  `releases_quarter`, and the tier test was rendered on a one-month window instead of the ladder's
  three-month window. The document's own `meta.covers` still lists `releases_quarter`.
- **Evidence — source.** `payouts.extended.yaml`, `payouts_ext_claim_reserve_release`,
  `factors[].id == routine_reserve_measure`:
  - tier 1 `when`: "the account settles only when the host asks and **no reserve has been freed from it in the last three months**"
  - tier 2 `when`: "the account settles only when the host asks and **a reserve has been freed from it in the last three months**"
  - `compute`: `{"releases_quarter": "COUNT('payouts_ledger', within_months=3, date_field='entry_date', event_type='payouts_reserve_released')"}` and
    `{"routine_standing": "routine_hold_all if (settles_on_request and releases_quarter == 0) else (routine_hold_quarter if (settles_on_request and releases_quarter > 0) else routine_hold_month)"}`
  - the same policy's `rule`: "where the account settles only when the host asks and no reserve has been freed from it in the last three months, every routine reserve ever taken on the account counts as standing; where the account settles only when the host asks and a reserve has been freed from it in the last three months, only the routine reserves taken in the three months up to that day count as standing"
- **Evidence — document.** Four places, all one month:
  1. table column header: `| How the account settles | Reserves freed **in the month up to that day** | The routine reserves that count as standing |`
  2. *Points of judgement*: "An account that settles only when the host asks and has had nothing freed from it **this month**."
  3. *Points of judgement*: "The same account once a reserve has been freed from it **in the month up to that day**."
  4. *On hypothetical figures*: "Where nothing has been freed from it **this month** the routine reserve standing is 900.00 USD; where something has been freed from it **this month** it is 500.00 USD".
- **Affected document and location.** `docs/payouts/which_routine_reserves_count_as_standing_b4e2adac.json`
  — the table's second column and the three restatements listed above. The row *methods* ("every routine
  reserve ever taken", "the three months up to that day", "the month up to that day") are correct; it is
  the test that selects between them that is wrong.
- **Consequence.** On an account settling only when the host asks with a reserve freed between one and
  three months before the handling day, the document sends the reader to tier 1 (the whole history of
  routine reserves) where the source sends them to tier 2 (three months only). The routine reserve standing,
  the sum kept back out of the release, and therefore the release entry itself come out wrong. Task 0 is
  unaffected in its number — the account has never had a reserve freed, so both readings select tier 1 and
  200.24 either way — but the defect is in the domain of a policy this task's tree depends on, and the skill
  records a changed tier condition even where the current numbers survive.
- **Relation to previous revisions.** First revision of this file; no earlier revision exists.

Everything else in the domain — all other 22 ladders, the three baselines, every base clause, all 13
retirements, all 57 tier parameters, the nine evidence contracts and the three state contracts — is
equivalent at the level of entailment.

## dependency_form

**KB-EXPLICIT RED — one finding, in a computation document of this task's tree. The prerequisite form
itself is clean.**

### What is clean

- **Both prerequisite sentences stand verbatim on the blocked side, in the state form the source declared**,
  and each appears in exactly one document in the corpus. Their same-document, same-form restatements
  ("While any such reserve … the drawable sum is not yet a settled figure"; "Until each such recovery …
  the sum freed is not yet a settled figure") are the source's own form and are not findings.
- **No state-form sentence is restated as an action.** Neither hub names the performer, the act or the
  policy that brings the waited-on state about.
- **No other problem's tool name appears anywhere.** Each of the five task tools is named in exactly one
  document — its own hub, in that hub's own invocation block. The draw hub does not name
  `release_claim_reserve_fb50cb2e`; the release hub does not name `post_recovery_correction_f20745c1`.
- **No route, no aggregated chain, no ordered cross-problem step list, no dependency table, no roadmap,
  no checklist.** No document mentions more than one of the five problems.
- **No wrong-versus-right contrast, no named mistake, no cross-problem example or FAQ.** The illustrations
  in every factor and baseline document are arithmetic on hypothetical figures within that document's own
  quantity.
- **No factor document says which tier a customer falls on**, or describes a reading to avoid, or writes
  any evidence row in as a fact. Each states its ladder as a rule and leaves the tier to the records.
- **Titles and openings name general subjects**: "Drawing Money From a Keyturn Host Payout Account on
  Request", "Keyturn Host Payout Account: Freeing a Claim Reserve", "Putting a Deductible Recovery Right on
  the Keyturn Host Payout Account", "Settlement Basis for a Draw From a Keyturn Host Payout Account". None
  mirrors a caller's situation, and the request type of the `on_request` draw policy is that policy's own
  general subject.
- **Findability without borrowed phrasing.** The depended-on documents were reached in the blind audit from
  the words the records and the prerequisite sentences use — "reserve", "open claim", "release entry",
  "deductible recovery", "correcting entry" — not from wording unique to the blocking document.

### E1. The computation document hedges its own baseline value

- **Statement.** *Settlement Basis for a Draw From a Keyturn Host Payout Account*
  (`working_out_a_requested_draw_5a9b35d4.json`), "The four amounts taken off", item 3:

  > "**As a returned transfer fee.** No returned transfer fee is taken from the drawable sum; the fee owed
  > stands at 0.00 USD, **and where a fee is owed it is taken off the drawable sum itself** rather than
  > booked as a deduction of its own, so the sum that leaves is already net of it."

- **Why it is a finding.** The corpus is meant to be a discrete topology in which the computation document
  states one standard method and one set of default values and is silent about any variation, so that the
  existence of a factor is discovered only from the customer's records. The conditional "where a fee is
  owed", placed immediately after the assertion that no fee is owed and the default of 0.00 USD, tells the
  reader that the default is not invariant and that some accounts do owe one. The three sibling items carry
  no such conditional — item 1 is "Nothing is withheld … the share withheld stands at 0 percent", item 2 is
  "No part of the payable balance is kept back … the share kept back stands at 0 percent", item 4 states
  its 25 percent flatly — so the hedge stands out as the one place the baseline is qualified.
- **It exceeds the document's source.** `payouts_ext_requested_draw.baseline.rule` says only: *"No returned
  transfer fee is taken from the drawable sum."* The conditional clause comes from the policy's full
  `rule`, where it is the `replaced_by` of the `overwrite` on `payouts_evt_deductions`
  ("Transfer fees are deductions in their own right…"): *"The returned transfer fee still owed is taken off
  the drawable sum itself rather than booked as a deduction of its own, so the sum that leaves is already
  net of it."*
- **The semantics is not missing elsewhere.** The same `replaced_by` content is also carried by the factor
  document *The Returned Transfer Fee Still Owed on a Keyturn Host Payout Account*: "The fee is a flat sum
  rather than a share, and it is taken off the drawable sum itself." So what this finding reports is the
  hedge in the baseline document, not an absent semantics; the report names the statement and what it
  carries and stops there.
- **Affected document and location.** `docs/payouts/working_out_a_requested_draw_5a9b35d4.json`, item 3 of
  "The four amounts taken off".
- **Consequence.** The solution is unaffected — the reader still needs the records and the factor document
  to learn that one return in twelve months makes the fee 20.00 USD — but a reader of the baseline alone
  learns that a variation exists, which is a discovery the corpus is meant to leave to the ledger.

### Examined and not recorded as findings

- *Settlement Basis for a Draw*, "Whichever stretch is measured, the reserve standing is never less than
  nothing…" — the phrase presupposes more than one stretch while the baseline states one, but it stands
  **verbatim in `payouts_ext_requested_draw.baseline.rule`**. The rendering is faithful; the hint
  originates on the policy side and is recorded below as a policy-side note, not as a KB verdict.
- *Reserve Accounting Basis*, "The two amounts taken off in step 5 are each worked out on their own base …"
  — an assembly statement that the `result` expression pins, naming no variation and no other document.
- *Reserve Bases*, "Releasing a reserve names the hold it releases, and a hold is released once and once
  only" — a **base** clause of `payouts_evt_reserve` in force, rendered as the source has it.
- *Terms on Moving … Between Schedules*, "The host must give the schedule's notice, and the change then
  takes effect the schedule's effective period after the notice is recorded" — a **base** clause of
  `payouts_schedule_change` that itself states an order; the KB may neither drop nor soften base law, so it
  is rendered and is not a finding of this scan.

## policy-side notes (recorded, and not affecting this skill's verdict)

1. **The draw's own baseline rule hints at variation.** `payouts_ext_requested_draw.baseline.rule` contains
   "Whichever stretch is measured, the reserve standing is never less than nothing", although the baseline
   states exactly one stretch. Any faithful rendering of that baseline inherits the hint.
2. **The release computation's standing-hold expression is looser than its own rule.** The rule says the
   standing claim hold is "every reserve taken against an open claim on the account, **less every reserve
   already freed from it**", but `release_taken` is `SUM('payouts_ledger','entry_amount',
   event_type='payouts_reserve_released')` over every release on the account, whether or not it named a
   claim reserve. The KB carries the rule's wording, so the looseness is source-side. It does not bite on
   this task (the account carries no release at the opening).
3. **Parameter definitions outlive the clauses that applied them.** `reserve_hold_days`,
   `reserve_release_trigger`, `negative_balance_grace_days`, `negative_balance_recovery_percent` and
   `tax_withholding_percent` remain in `parameter_schema` and in every variant while the base clauses that
   put them to work are retired by `overwrite`. The KB is right to render the parameters and right to mark
   the clauses retired, but a reader can reasonably ask what the surviving figures now govern.

## R1 — verified CLOSED

**The source, re-extracted from the parsed structure** (not from my round-1 notes):

```
T1 when  : the account settles only when the host asks and no reserve has been freed from it in the last three months
T1 method: every routine reserve ever taken on the account counts as standing
T2 when  : the account settles only when the host asks and a reserve has been freed from it in the last three months
T2 method: only the routine reserves taken in the three months up to that day count as standing
T3 when  : otherwise
T3 method: only the routine reserves taken in the month up to that day count as standing
releases_quarter = COUNT('payouts_ledger', within_months=3, date_field='entry_date', event_type='payouts_reserve_released')
routine_standing = routine_hold_all if (settles_on_request and releases_quarter == 0)
                   else (routine_hold_quarter if (settles_on_request and releases_quarter > 0) else routine_hold_month)
```

**The document now.** All four round-1 occurrences are corrected, and the fifth passage is an addition:

| 5 | — | new: "**A reserve freed more than three months before that day.** It stands outside the test the first two rows turn on, so an account settling only when the host asks with no release inside those three months sits in the first row however many releases stand further back." |

The renderer's claim that the **methods** were already correct and are unchanged is confirmed: the three

three months that are summed"). The added boundary point is a genuine other-side-of-the-threshold
statement, not a hint about any customer's tier: it names no account, no record and no outcome for this

### The sweep the renderer reported, re-run with my own oracle

I did not take the renderer's sweep on trust. My oracle is the one that actually caught R1 in round 1 —
the **forward** direction, which is the complete test for this class: *every temporal or threshold
expression occurring in any tier's `when` or `method` string must appear in that factor's own document*,
literally or through a declared equivalence where the render skill requires a business term to be rendered
as a figure ("a calendar quarter" → 92 calendar days, "for a year or longer" → 365, "two years or longer"
→ 730, "within the past week" → 7, "the schedule's grace period" → 14, "the documentation threshold" →
600.00 USD, "the schedule's qualifying number" → 10, "the tolerated number" → 1). Run over **all 23**
factors, against the extended policy file, with the compute windows printed alongside:

A **converse** pass was also run — every window phrase the document asserts, traced back to the ladder —

**The `replaced_by` semantics is still carried.** Overwrite #9 retires "Transfer fees are deductions in

transfer fee still owed is taken off the drawable sum itself rather than booked as a deduction of its own,

|---|---|

| one draw writes one entry | *Drawing Money … on Request*: "One draw sends money out of the account … and books **a single new transfer entry** out of the account." |
| the sum that leaves is already net of it | *Drawing Money … on Request*: "what leaves the account is the drawable sum", with the baseline's assembly |
